title: FDA Oncology Approval Notices in October 2026: Complete List
summary: All seven FDA oncology approval notices in October 2026, with dates, treatment settings, key trial evidence and approved or late-stage competing options.
body_markdown:
Seven FDA oncology approval notices were dated October 1-31, 2026. They cover previously untreated CLL/SLL, breast-cancer maintenance, adjuvant colon cancer, bladder-preserving treatment, locally advanced rectal cancer, previously treated TMB-high solid tumors and hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The main pattern is a change in where established medicines compete: earlier treatment, maintenance and biomarker-defined populations.


Updated: November 3, 2026


The complete list below includes every notice dated October 1-31 in the FDA oncology approval-notification index, rechecked November 3. FDA notes that the index does not announce every oncology approval or label update.[\[1\]](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/oncology-cancerhematologic-malignancies-approval-notifications)


Notice date Medicine Treatment setting and eligibility


October 2, 2026 Pirtobrutinib (Jaypirca) Previously untreated adult CLL/SLL, with no known 17p deletion


October 7, 2026 Tucatinib (Tukysa), with trastuzumab and pertuzumab Maintenance after induction in adults with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer


October 8, 2026 Atezolizumab (Tecentriq) or atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs (Tecentriq Hybreza), with a fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin Adjuvant Stage III dMMR colon cancer; formulation-specific age and weight criteria


October 14, 2026 Nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln (Anktiva), with BCG Adult BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer, expanded to high-grade papillary-only tumors


October 19, 2026 Dostarlimab (Jemperli) Adults with Stage II/III locally advanced MSI-H or dMMR rectal cancer; accelerated approval


October 22, 2026 Pembrolizumab (Keytruda) or pembrolizumab and berahyaluronidase alfa-pmph (Keytruda Qlex) Previously treated unresectable or metastatic TMB-high solid tumors, with a revised threshold of at least 13 mutations/Mb and no satisfactory alternatives


October 26, 2026 Talazoparib (Talzenna), with enzalutamide Adults with HRR-mutated metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naïve or -sensitive prostate cancer


Notice dates determine inclusion. The October 22 pembrolizumab entry reports an October 16 approval. Each paired-formulation notice counts once.


## Pirtobrutinib enters a crowded first-line CLL/SLL market


Pirtobrutinib's October 2 approval covers adults with previously untreated CLL/SLL and no known 17p deletion. BRUIN CLL-313 enrolled 282 patients and compared pirtobrutinib with bendamustine plus rituximab. The progression-free survival hazard ratio was 0.20; median PFS was not estimable with pirtobrutinib versus 33.5 months with the comparator. Overall-survival data were immature.[\[2\]](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-pirtobrutinib-previously-untreated-chronic-lymphocytic-leukemia-or-small-lymphocytic)


Approved competitors in this setting include zanubrutinib (Brukinsa) and acalabrutinib (Calquence) plus venetoclax (Venclexta). Both have randomized evidence in previously untreated CLL, including populations without 17p deletion.[\[3\]](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-zanubrutinib-chronic-lymphocytic-leukemia-or-small-lymphocytic-lymphoma)[\[4\]](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-acalabrutinib-venetoclax-chronic-lymphocytic-leukemia-or-small-lymphocytic-lymphoma) Venetoclax plus obinutuzumab (Gazyva) is another approved first-line regimen.[\[5\]](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2019/208573Orig1s013ltr.pdf) Pirtobrutinib therefore joins an established targeted-treatment field, while its pivotal comparison was against chemoimmunotherapy.


## Tucatinib competes at the maintenance transition


Tucatinib's October 7 approval adds it to trastuzumab and pertuzumab after induction for adults with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer. HER2CLIMB-05 enrolled 654 adults without progression after trastuzumab, pertuzumab and a taxane. Median PFS was 24.9 months with tucatinib versus 16.3 months with placebo, each on the antibody backbone; overall-survival data were immature.[\[6\]](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-tucatinib-trastuzumab-and-pertuzumab-maintenance-treatment-her2-positive-breast-cancer)


For the HR-positive subset, an approved competing maintenance regimen is palbociclib (Ibrance) plus trastuzumab, with or without pertuzumab, and endocrine therapy. Its June 2026 approval followed PATINA, which compared that regimen with the same antibody and endocrine backbone without palbociclib.[\[7\]](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-palbociclib-trastuzumab-or-without-pertuzumab-and-endocrine-therapy-maintenance) The two approvals address overlapping maintenance populations, but palbociclib's indication requires HR-positive disease.


## Atezolizumab adds immunotherapy after colon-cancer resection


The October 8 notice adds atezolizumab with a fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin for adjuvant Stage III dMMR colon cancer. Tecentriq eligibility starts at age two; Tecentriq Hybreza starts at age 12 and requires a weight of at least 40 kg. In ATOMIC, atezolizumab plus mFOLFOX6 followed by atezolizumab was compared with mFOLFOX6 alone after complete resection. The disease-free-survival hazard ratio was 0.50, with median DFS not reached in either arm.[\[8\]](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-atezolizumab-combination-chemotherapy-stage-iii-mismatch-repair-deficient-colon-cancer)


Chemotherapy remains the direct comparator: mFOLFOX6 comprises oxaliplatin, leucovorin and fluorouracil. Capecitabine (Xeloda), alone or as part of combination chemotherapy, is also approved for adjuvant Stage III colon cancer.[\[9\]](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/020896s044s051lbl.pdf) The late-stage immunotherapy competitor is dostarlimab in Phase 3 AZUR-2 for untreated, resectable T4N0 or Stage III dMMR/MSI-H colon cancer. That program gives dostarlimab before and after surgery, so it competes earlier in the surgical pathway than atezolizumab's postoperative indication.[\[10\]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05855200)


## Anktiva expands into papillary-only bladder cancer


Anktiva's October 14 notice expands its use with BCG to adults with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer containing high-grade papillary-only tumors. The prior indication required carcinoma in situ, with or without papillary tumors. FDA concluded that the earlier efficacy demonstration in CIS-containing disease could be extrapolated to high-grade papillary disease.[\[11\]](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-expanded-indication-nogapendekin-alfa-inbakicept-pmln-bcg-unresponsive-non-muscle)


A competing late-stage option is TAR-210, the erdafitinib intravesical delivery system, in Phase 3 MoonRISe-3. It enrolls adults with susceptible FGFR alterations and papillary-only high-risk NMIBC (high-grade Ta or any T1, without CIS) after BCG who are ineligible for or refuse radical cystectomy. Eligible groups include BCG-unresponsive, BCG-experienced and BCG-intolerant patients. The randomized trial compares TAR-210 with investigator's choice of intravesical gemcitabine or mitomycin C.[\[12\]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06919965) Gemcitabine intravesical system (Inlexzo) is already approved in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with CIS, with or without papillary tumors. Its approved population overlaps Anktiva's broader indication but does not cover papillary-only disease.[\[13\]](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-gemcitabine-intravesical-system-non-muscle-invasive-bladder-cancer)


## Dostarlimab creates an approved rectal-cancer immunotherapy option


Dostarlimab received accelerated approval on October 19 for adults with Stage II/III locally advanced MSI-H or dMMR rectal cancer. AZUR-1 evaluated 154 patients; those achieving a clinical complete response entered non-operative monitoring, while incomplete response, recurrence or progression could lead to standard treatment. FDA reported a sustained 12-month clinical complete response rate of 47% among 116 patients evaluable by independent central review, alongside supportive investigator-led evidence.[\[14\]](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-grants-accelerated-approval-dostarlimab-locally-advanced-rectal-cancer)


The competing approved chemotherapy option is capecitabine as a component of perioperative chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced rectal cancer.[\[9\]](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/020896s044s051lbl.pdf) FOLFOX and CAPEOX, built around oxaliplatin with fluorouracil or capecitabine, are established chemotherapy options in Stage II/III treatment pathways.[\[15\]](https://www.cancer.gov/types/colorectal/hp/rectal-treatment-pdq) These regimens are broader than the dMMR/MSI-H population.


## Pembrolizumab narrows the TMB-high eligibility threshold


The pembrolizumab notice is dated October 22 in the index and reports an October 16 action. FDA converted the TMB-high solid-tumor indication to traditional approval and raised the threshold from at least 10 to at least 13 mutations/Mb. It covers adult and pediatric patients with unresectable or metastatic disease after prior treatment and no satisfactory alternatives. In KEYNOTE-158 patients with TMB of at least 13 mutations/Mb, the objective response rate was 36%; efficacy supporting traditional approval was not confirmed for TMB of 10 to below 13 mutations/Mb.[\[16\]](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-grants-traditional-approval-pembrolizumab-or-pembrolizumab-and-berahyaluronidase-alfa-pmph)


Approved alternatives depend on an additional qualifying biomarker or tumor type. Dostarlimab has accelerated approval for previously treated dMMR recurrent or advanced solid tumors with no satisfactory alternatives.[\[17\]](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/761174s015lbl.pdf) Nivolumab plus ipilimumab is approved for unresectable or metastatic MSI-H/dMMR colorectal cancer in patients aged 12 or older.[\[18\]](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-nivolumab-ipilimumab-unresectable-or-metastatic-msi-h-or-dmmr-colorectal-cancer) These are competing options for overlapping eligible patients, not interchangeable labels.


## Talazoparib expands PARP competition in hormone-sensitive prostate cancer


Talazoparib's October 26 approval adds it to enzalutamide for adults with HRR-mutated metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naïve or -sensitive prostate cancer. In TALAPRO-3, 599 patients received enzalutamide with talazoparib or placebo, alongside ongoing androgen deprivation. The radiographic PFS hazard ratio was 0.48; median rPFS was not reached with talazoparib versus 45.8 months with placebo. Overall-survival data were immature.[\[19\]](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-talazoparib-enzalutamide-metastatic-androgen-pathway-modulation-naive-or-sensitive)


The approved PARP-based competitor is niraparib plus abiraterone acetate (Akeega) with prednisone, whose hormone-sensitive indication is limited to BRCA2-mutated disease.[\[20\]](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-niraparib-and-abiraterone-acetate-plus-prednisone-brca2-mutated-metastatic-castration) Enzalutamide with androgen deprivation is also an approved option in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer, without an HRR-mutation requirement.[\[21\]](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/203415s026lbl.pdf) Talazoparib's broader HRR eligibility makes the gene-level overlap with Akeega central to the competitive comparison.


## Final Perspective


October's seven notices change several distinct treatment decisions: initial systemic therapy, maintenance, postoperative treatment and organ-preserving care. The strongest direct competitive overlaps are first-line CLL/SLL, HER2-positive breast-cancer maintenance and hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, where named targeted regimens are already approved.


The bladder, rectal and tumor-agnostic notices require closer attention to histology and biomarkers. Papillary-only NMIBC, dMMR/MSI-H rectal cancer and the revised TMB threshold each define a different eligible population, even when the same drugs appear in a broader disease landscape.


This focus on defined patient populations extends the precision-treatment trend discussed in Maven's[2025 FDA approvals analysis](https://mavenbio.com/research/fda-drug-approvals-in-2025-what-the-year-s-46-new-therapies-reveal-about-industry-direction) .
